data.narrative:
Cobod, a Series A housing and construction technology company, has raised $46M to date. The comp universe consists of two private peers—Inversion Space and Material Evolution—reflecting the nascent state of the frontier-tech construction sector, with no directly comparable public companies available for benchmarking.

A stage-progression methodology forms the basis of valuation analysis, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to post-Series A transitions. Using the $46M total raised as a valuation proxy, this approach yields an implied valuation of $92M. This single-method triangulation produces a range anchored at $92M median, with a low bound of $78M (15% haircut) and a high bound of $106M (15% premium).

The valuation of $78M–$106M, with a central case of $92M, reflects material uncertainty inherent in a single methodological approach and a sparse comp set. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific sector and stage, the representativeness of private peers given the frontier-tech nature of the market, and execution risk in an early-stage venture. Further refinement would benefit from comparable transaction data, revenue or unit economics if available, and explicit margin assumptions for the construction technology segment.
